Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We will show that the minimum possible value is \(\boxed{499}\).

---

## 1. Structural decomposition of the sets

If \(d\mid e\), then

\[
|A_d\cap A_e|=d=|A_d|,
\]

so

\[
A_d\subseteq A_e.
\]

Thus for any \(i,j\),

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

For each positive integer \(n\), define

\[
B_n=A_n\setminus \bigcup_{\substack{d\mid n\\ d<n}} A_d.
\]

If \(x\in B_n\) and \(x\in A_m\), then

\[
x\in A_n\cap A_m=A_{\gcd(n,m)}.
\]

Since \(x\notin A_d\) for any proper divisor \(d\) of \(n\), we must have \(\gcd(n,m)=n\), so \(n\mid m\). Hence the sets \(B_n\) are pairwise disjoint, and

\[
A_n=\bigsqcup_{d\mid n}B_d.
\]

Because \(|A_n|=n\), we get

\[
\sum_{d\mid n}|B_d|=n,
\]

so by Möbius inversion (or induction using \(\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d)=n\)),

\[
|B_d|=\varphi(d).
\]

For the divisors of \(250=2\cdot 5^3\), the relevant block sizes are:

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d & 1 & 2 & 5 & 10 & 25 & 50 & 125 & 250\\
\hline
|B_d| & 1 & 1 & 4 & 4 & 20 & 20 & 100 & 100
\end{array}
\]

The quantity to minimize is

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max_{e\mid d}\max B_e.
\]

---

## 2. Reduction to a permutation of the eight blocks

The set \(A_{250}\) is exactly the disjoint union of the eight blocks \(B_d\) with \(d\mid 250\), and it has \(250\) elements. Relabel the elements of \(A_{250}\) as \(1,2,\dots,250\) in increasing order. This cannot increase any maximum, so we may assume the eight blocks partition \(\{1,\dots,250\}\).

Now sort the blocks by their largest element, and replace each block by a consecutive interval of the same size in that order. If the sorted blocks have sizes \(s_1,\dots,s_8\) and cumulative sums \(S_k=s_1+\cdots+s_k\), then the \(k\)-th block originally had largest element at least \(S_k\), so this replacement cannot increase any \(\max A_d\).

Thus it suffices to minimize over all permutations of the eight blocks.

Let \(M_d\) be the total size of all blocks up to and including the last block whose label divides \(d\). Then the desired sum is \(\sum_{d\mid 250}M_d\).

By exchange arguments:

- Block \(1\) must be first, since it is contained in every \(A_d\).
- Block \(250\) must be last, since it only appears in \(A_{250}\), whose maximum is always \(250\).

So we only need to order the six blocks

\[
2,\ 5,\ 10,\ 25,\ 50,\ 125,
\]

with sizes

\[
1,\ 4,\ 4,\ 20,\ 20,\ 100.
\]

Let their completion times within these six blocks be:

\[
t_2,\ t_5,\ t_{10},\ t_{25},\ t_{50},\ t_{125}.
\]

Then the total sum is

\[
1+250+\bigl(1+t_2+1+t_5+1+\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})+1+\max(t_5,t_{25})+1+\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10},t_{25},t_{50})+1+\max(t_5,t_{25},t_{125})\bigr).
\]

Equivalently, if

\[
T=t_2+t_5+\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})+\max(t_5,t_{25})
+\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10},t_{25},t_{50})
+\max(t_5,t_{25},t_{125}),
\]

then the required sum is

\[
257+T.
\]

---

## 3. Lower bound for \(T\)

### Case 1: Block \(125\) is not after all of \(2,5,10,25,50\)

Then the maximum among \(2,5,10,25,50\) is at least the total size of those five blocks plus block \(125\):

\[
\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10},t_{25},t_{50})=149.
\]

Also,

\[
\max(t_5,t_{25},t_{125})\ge 4+20+100=124.
\]

Furthermore,

\[
t_2\ge 1,\qquad t_5\ge 4,\qquad \max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})\ge 9,\qquad \max(t_5,t_{25})\ge 24.
\]

Thus

\[
T\ge 1+4+9+24+149+124=311.
\]

---

### Case 2: Block \(125\) is after all of \(2,5,10,25,50\)

Then

\[
\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10},t_{25},t_{50})=49
\]

and

\[
\max(t_5,t_{25},t_{125})=149.
\]

So we only need to minimize

\[
H=t_2+t_5+\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})+\max(t_5,t_{25}).
\]

Block \(50\) does not appear in \(H\), so moving it to the end of the five blocks cannot increase \(H\). Assume \(50\) is last.

Now consider blocks \(2,5,10,25\).

If block \(25\) is not last among them, then

\[
\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})\ge 29.
\]

Also, for blocks of sizes \(4\) and \(20\),

\[
t_5+\max(t_5,t_{25})\ge 28.
\]

Together with \(t_2\ge 1\), this gives

\[
H\ge 1+28+29=58.
\]

If block \(25\) is last, then

\[
\max(t_2,t_5,t_{10})=9,\qquad \max(t_5,t_{25})=29.
\]

The minimum possible value of \(t_2+t_5\) is \(1+5=6\), achieved by ordering \(2,5,10\). Therefore

\[
H\ge 6+9+29=44.
\]

Hence in this case,

\[
T\ge 44+49+149=242.
\]

Since Case 1 gives \(T\ge 311\), overall

\[
T\ge 242.
\]

Therefore the desired sum is at least

\[
257+242=499.
\]

---

## 4. Construction achieving \(499\)

Take the blocks for divisors of \(250\) to be consecutive intervals in the order

\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250:
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
B_1&=\{1\},\\
B_2&=\{2\},\\
B_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
B_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
B_{25}&=\{11,12,\dots,30\},\\
B_{50}&=\{31,32,\dots,50\},\\
B_{125}&=\{51,52,\dots,150\},\\
B_{250}&=\{151,152,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For every positive integer \(n\nmid 250\), choose \(B_n\) to be any disjoint set of \(\varphi(n)\) positive integers larger than \(250\).

Now define

\[
A_m=\bigsqcup_{d\mid m}B_d.
\]

Then

\[
|A_m|=\sum_{d\mid m}\varphi(d)=m,
\]

and

\[
A_i\cap A_j=\bigsqcup_{d\mid \gcd(i,j)}B_d=A_{\gcd(i,j)},
\]

so the condition is satisfied.

The relevant maxima are:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\max A_1&=1,\\
\max A_2&=2,\\
\max A_5&=6,\\
\max A_{10}&=10,\\
\max A_{25}&=30,\\
\max A_{50}&=50,\\
\max A_{125}&=150,\\
\max A_{250}&=250.
\end{aligned}
\]

Their sum is

\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}.
\]
